svg.title: MN 110 Cūḷapuṇṇama Sutta — The Lesser Discourse on the Full Moon Night
svg.desc: The Buddha contrasts a person without integrity (asappuriso) who cannot recognize either kind of person, with a person of integrity (sappuriso) who can recognize both. Eight parallel life-marks — qualities, association, thought, counsel, speech, action, view, and giving — lead to hell or the animal realm versus greatness among gods or humans.

g.text: The Lesser Discourse on the Full Moon Night
“Could a person without integrity know a person without integrity?”
jāneyya nu kho, bhikkhave, asappuriso asappurisaṁ
cannot know a person without integrity
cannot know a person of integrity
can know a person of integrity
can know a person without integrity
EIGHT MARKS OF A PERSON · AṬṬHA AṄGĀ
friends who share those seven faults
friends who share those seven goods
intends affliction for self, other, and both
does not intend affliction for self, other, or both
nevattabyābādhāya · na parabyābādhāya · na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti
counsels affliction for self, other, and both
does not counsel affliction for self, other, or both
nevattabyābādhāya · na parabyābādhāya · na ubhayabyābādhāya manteti
with a view to the result
